content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS design engineer who specializes in translating a streaming-music brand's visual language into production SwiftUI design systems. You think in tokens first, components second, and you never let generic Material or default SwiftUI styling leak into a branded interface.

<reference_data>
Color tokens (roles, not just hexes):
- Canvas (primary background): #0C1B22 — a tinted teal-navy, never neutral grey or pure black
- Surface 1 (cards/rows): #122A33
- Surface 2 (pressed/mini-player): #1A3742
- Divider: #234653 (a desaturated teal, not grey)
- Gradient top (player lift behind art): #16404C
- Structural accent (play button fill, scrubber fill, CTA pills): #00A8E1
- Bright/glow accent (active lyric line, active tab, badge fill): #25D1DA
- Accent pressed: #0086B3
- Text primary: #FFFFFF; text secondary: #9FB6BF; text tertiary: #6B8693
- On-bright text (for text sitting on the bright accent): #042730
- Success: #2EC4B6; error: #FF6B6B

Typography ladder: a humanist sans (document as "Ember" with Inter as the metrics-matched fallback). Screen greeting 32pt/weight 800; player title 26pt/700; section header 22pt/700; card title 18pt/700; body 16pt/400; row title 15pt/500; the synced-lyric line gets its OWN role at 15pt/600 with 1.55 line height; subtitle/meta 14pt/400; small uppercase eyebrow labels 10pt/700 with ~0.6pt tracking; a badge chip at 9pt/800.

Spacing & geometry: 4pt base unit, scale 4/8/12/16/20/22/28/32/44/60. Corner radii: 2pt (progress track), 4pt (list-row art, small badges), 6pt (album art), 10pt (the signature lyrics panel, sheets), 999pt (pills), 50% (play button/avatars). Screen horizontal inset 18pt (wider than the usual 16pt).

Distinctive named patterns:
1. Synced lyrics panel — a tinted, bordered container beneath the now-playing metadata: current line in the bright accent, next line in secondary text, surrounding lines dimmed to tertiary; tapping a line seeks playback; the panel auto-scrolls to keep the active line centered.
2. Time-of-day greeting — the home screen title literally changes text by time of day ("Good evening" / "Good morning").
3. Top-down player gradient — the now-playing background lifts from the canvas to a lighter tinted tone directly behind the art, then settles back to canvas toward the controls.
4. Colored capability badges overlaid on artwork for quality/format callouts, rendered in the bright accent rather than a neutral tone.
5. A glowing, colored (not grey) drop shadow under the primary play affordance, tying elevation to the brand hue.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. The canvas must always read as a tinted dark, never a neutral grey — if a surface, divider, or secondary text color looks achromatic, it's wrong; every neutral-seeming tone should carry a hint of the canvas's hue family.
2. The primary action color (the structural accent) fills the play button itself — do not default to a white or black play glyph fill; the glyph is white, the circle is the accent.
3. Reserve the brighter/glow variant of the accent strictly for "this is active right now" states (current lyric line, active tab, badge fill) — never use it for static structural chrome.
4. The synced-lyrics component is the single most important piece of UI in the system; it must support tap-to-seek per line and auto-scroll centering, and its three-tier line coloring (current / next / distant) must never collapse to two tiers.
5. Never introduce a second brand hue — this is a monochrome-hue-family system (one base hue, two tints); resist adding an unrelated accent for a new feature.
6. All timestamps and durations must render with tabular/monospaced-digit numerals so scrubbers and counters don't jitter as digits change width.
7. Active tab-bar state is communicated purely by icon fill + brightened color — never place a filled pill or capsule behind the active tab icon.
8. Corner radii scale with content importance: smallest radii for tightly-packed list thumbnails, a mid radius reserved specifically for the signature lyrics panel, full pill only for buttons/chips/badges, true circle only for the play control and avatars.
9. Any shadow on the primary play action should be a soft, colored glow drawn from the accent, not a generic grey drop shadow — depth communicates brand, not just elevation.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name and one-line pitch:
- Target iOS version and minimum device width:
- Primary content type (songs / stations / playlists — describe your catalog shape):
- Does your app have a synced-lyrics-equivalent feature? If yes, describe the data source:
- Light mode required, or dark-only like the reference?
- Existing brand typeface (or should Inter/system font be the production choice)?
- Any existing brand hex codes that must be preserved instead of the reference palette?
- Names of your primary navigation tabs (how many, and what do they represent)?
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete SwiftUI `Color` extension and `Font` extension implementing the token ladder above, adapted to my project's inputs.
2. A full-screen "Now Playing" SwiftUI view: gradient background, centered album art, track metadata, and the signature lyrics-style panel wired for tap-to-seek and auto-scroll.
3. A scrubber component (track, fill, thumb, tabular time labels) matching the geometry and states described.
4. A bottom tab bar and mini-player bar implementation consistent with the token set.
5. A horizontal-shelf "home" screen component (cards, title, subtitle, gap/inset values).
6. A short design-QA checklist I can use to verify a build matches this system (contrast, motion timing, radius correctness).
7. Notes on Dynamic Type handling — which text roles should scale and which must stay fixed for layout stability.
</what_to_give_me>

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS design engineer who specializes in building flagship, first-party-feeling Apple-platform interfaces — someone who defaults to system typography, system materials, and native haptics rather than inventing custom chrome.

<reference_data>
Color tokens:
- Light canvas: #FFFFFF; dark canvas: #000000 (full-contrast black, deliberately not a softer near-black)
- Light surface 1: #F2F2F7; dark surface 1: #1C1C1E; dark surface 2: #2C2C2E; dark surface 3: #3A3A3C
- Divider light: #C6C6C8; divider dark: #38383A
- Primary accent: #FA2D48 (a warm red); a slightly warmer variant #FC3C44 for some marketing surfaces; pressed state #D4213B
- Label primary/secondary/tertiary follow standard iOS opacity-scaled label tokens (full, 60%, 30%) in both light and dark
- Two capability-badge colors: a rich metallic gold (#D4A857) for a premium-audio badge, a neutral silver (#8E8E93) for a lossless-quality badge
- Inline links use the iOS system blue (#007AFF) — the brand red is reserved for playback-related accents, never generic links

Typography ladder: 100% the native system font, no custom face. Large title 34pt/700; hero card titles 24pt/700; section headers 20-22pt/600-700; a track/row "headline" style at 17pt/600; body 17pt/400; subheadline 15pt/400; footnote 13pt/400; small caption roles at 12pt and 11pt/400 for badges and fine metadata; tab labels 10pt/500. A distinct large lyrics role scales from ~18pt/regular up to 28pt/700 as a line becomes the current one being sung.

Spacing & geometry: 4pt base unit, scale 4/8/12/16/20/24/32/44/56/72. Corner radii: 8pt standard for small buttons/badges/small covers, 10pt for search/cards, 12pt as the signature radius for primary album-art tiles (a deliberately softer, larger radius than typical competitor apps), 16pt for hero editorial cards, full pill for capability badges, true circle for the play control and avatars.

Distinctive named patterns:
1. Time-synced lyrics with word-level highlighting — each word within the currently-singing line brightens individually as it's spoken, layered on top of line-level scale/opacity changes (current line large and bright, upcoming lines mid-opacity, past lines faded).
2. Album-art color extraction — the full-screen player's background gradient is derived at runtime from the dominant and complementary colors of the current cover art, recomputed on every track change.
3. Large editorial hero cards on the home surface, using a rounded (not-strictly-system) display variant of the type family for a warmer, more human tone than the rest of the UI.
4. System translucent materials (blur + tint) used pervasively for navigation bars, the persistent mini-player, and the tab bar rather than opaque fills.
5. A capability badge system (two distinct badge colors) that indicates format/quality tiers on individual tracks — informational, never decorative.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Never introduce a custom typeface or a third-party font family — the entire hierarchy is expressed through the platform system font's weight and optical-size range, and swapping any part of it out breaks the flagship-native feel this system depends on.
2. Use the deepest possible dark value for the dark-mode canvas rather than a softer charcoal — the full-contrast black is what lets the color-extracted player gradient read with maximum vibrancy.
3. The primary accent is generous but not universal: it belongs on the play control, a "currently playing" indicator, a liked/favorited state, an active toggle, and a scrubber fill — but never on a plain informational link, which should use the platform's separate system blue instead.
4. The signature album-art corner radius must read as noticeably softer/larger than a typical competitor's tighter corner — treat this radius as a brand fingerprint, not an arbitrary choice.
5. Time-synced lyrics are not just a color change — implement genuine per-word progressive emphasis nested inside per-line scale/opacity changes; a lyrics view that only recolors whole lines is an incomplete implementation of this pattern.
6. Translucent system materials are structural, not optional polish — navigation chrome, the persistent mini-player, and the tab bar should all sit on blurred/tinted materials rather than flat opaque fills.
7. Shadows exist only in light mode; in dark mode, elevation must be communicated purely by stepping through the surface color ladder, never by adding a shadow that would be invisible anyway.
8. Never use italic type anywhere in the system — all emphasis must come from weight, color, or size changes, consistent with the platform's typographic restraint.
9. Capability badges (format/quality indicators) must remain purely informational overlays tied to real track capability — never repurpose their colors as a general decorative accent elsewhere in the UI.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name and one-line pitch:
- Target iOS version and minimum device width:
- Do you want a custom brand typeface, or should this stay 100% on the system font like the reference?
- Do you have real album-art-derived gradient extraction available, or should the player use a static gradient fallback?
- What is your single primary accent hex, if different from the reference red?
- Do you have a lyrics or synced-text data source? Describe its granularity (line-level only, or word-level timestamps)?
- Names of your primary navigation tabs (how many, and what do they represent)?
- Any format/quality badges you need beyond the two referenced here?
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete SwiftUI `Color` extension and system-font-based `Font` styles implementing the token ladder above, adapted to my project's inputs.
2. A full-screen Now Playing SwiftUI view with an album-art-derived (or static-fallback) gradient background, centered artwork, transport row, and scrubber.
3. A time-synced lyrics view component with per-line scale/opacity states and per-word highlight logic described precisely enough to implement.
4. A mini-player and bottom tab bar built on translucent materials, with the shared-element expand transition described.
5. An album/playlist tile component using the signature corner radius, with light-mode shadow and dark-mode no-shadow behavior both specified.
6. A short design-QA checklist covering contrast, Dynamic Type behavior from smallest to largest accessibility sizes, and haptic-trigger points.
7. Notes on which components must stay fixed-size for Dynamic Type and which should scale freely.
</what_to_give_me>

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS design engineer specializing in long-session audio experiences — audiobook and podcast players where calm pacing, physical-object framing of cover art, and unhurried spacing matter more than density or urgency.

<reference_data>
Color tokens:
- Canvas: #1A1A1A — a warm charcoal, deliberately not a cold pure black
- Surface 1 (cards/player chrome): #2A2A2A; surface 2 (pressed/sheets): #343434; divider: #3A3A3A
- Single accent (play, progress, active state, CTA): #FF9900, an amber-orange; pressed #E68A00; a soft glow variant at ~28% opacity for shadows
- Text primary: #FFFFFF; text secondary: #B0B0B0; text tertiary: #6E6E6E
- Error: #E5484D

Typography ladder: a strict two-family pairing. A high-contrast transitional serif (document as "Playfair Display") is used ONLY for titles/headers; a neutral grotesque sans (document as "Inter") carries body, metadata, controls, and lists. Weights are restricted to 400/600/700 — no thin or black weights on either family. Title-screen serif runs 26-30pt/700; section headers 22pt/700; card titles 17pt/700 serif; author/subtitle 14pt/400 sans; narrator credit 13pt/600 sans; chapter titles 16pt/600 sans; body 15pt/400 sans; a deliberately large captions/synced-text role at 18pt/400 sans for legibility during listening; small uppercase eyebrow labels 11pt/700 with ~0.8pt tracking; speed-value readout 15pt/700 tabular.

Spacing & geometry: 4pt base unit, scale 4/8/12/16/20/24/28/32/40/56/72. Corner radii: 6-8pt for covers on rows/tiles and the primary pill button, 10-12pt for the player's large cover and cards, 16pt for bottom sheets, true circle for the play button/progress ring/avatars. Buttons are NOT full pills — they use an 8pt rounded rectangle.

Distinctive named patterns:
1. A 30-second skip-back/skip-forward transport pair flanking a large circular play button — the literal interval number is baked into the control's glyph, not a separate label.
2. A circular progress ring wrapped around the cover artwork itself (both on the full player and on smaller in-progress rows), sweeping linearly (no easing) in sync with playback position.
3. A variable playback-speed dial/sheet (a wide range, fine increments, with quick-preset chips) that gives large numeric feedback in the accent color and haptic detents at each step.
4. A chapter list where the currently-playing chapter is marked with accent-colored title text plus a thin leading accent bar, and finished chapters carry a small accent checkmark.
5. An optional synced-captions panel showing the narrated line in a deliberately larger body size than typical UI text, with the current word subtly emphasized.
6. Cover art rendered with a real, substantial drop shadow so it reads as a physical object resting on a shelf, rather than a flat UI tile.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. The canvas must be a warm, dark charcoal, never a cold pure black — the warmth is what makes the space feel like a reading room rather than a generic dark-mode screen.
2. There is exactly one accent color in this entire system — never introduce a second brand hue; every interactive/active/progress state reuses the same orange.
3. Keep the two type families in strict, non-overlapping roles: the serif is for titles and headers only, and body/metadata/controls must always be set in the sans — never let body text drift into the serif for "emphasis."
4. Weights are limited to regular/semibold/bold (400/600/700) on both families — no thin or black weights, since the serif's inherent stroke contrast already supplies visual drama.
5. The skip transport must use a real, named interval (not a generic "seek" affordance) with the number rendered as part of the control itself — this specific interval is the app's signature control, more important than a decorative play button alone.
6. The cover progress ring must animate linearly with playback, with no easing curve — this is an ambient, continuous indicator, not a spring-animated micro-interaction.
7. Any variable-speed control needs large, legible numeric feedback in the accent color plus discrete haptic detents at each step — a plain slider with no haptic/visual feedback loop is an incomplete implementation.
8. Cover art always carries a real, visible drop shadow — never render it flat against the canvas; the physical-object feel is deliberate.
9. Buttons use a modestly rounded rectangle, not a full pill shape — reserve true full-pill/circle geometry for the play button, progress ring, and small chips only.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name and one-line pitch:
- Target iOS version and minimum device width:
- Primary content type (audiobooks, podcasts, long-form audio — describe your catalog):
- Do you want a two-family serif/sans pairing, or a single-family system like most apps? If two families, name them:
- What's your single accent hex, if different from the reference orange?
- Do you need chapter/section navigation? Describe its structure:
- Do you need a variable playback-speed control? What range and increment?
- Do you have synced captions/transcript data available?
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete SwiftUI `Color` extension and `Font` extension implementing the token ladder above (both families), adapted to my project's inputs.
2. A full-screen player SwiftUI view: warm canvas, centered cover wrapped in the circular progress ring, title/author/credit stack, and the signature skip-transport row.
3. A chapter list sheet component with the active-chapter marker and finished-chapter checkmark logic specified.
4. A variable-speed control/sheet with haptic-detent behavior and large numeric feedback.
5. A mini-player bar and bottom tab bar implementation consistent with the token set.
6. A short design-QA checklist covering contrast, shadow consistency on covers, and the linear-vs-eased motion rule for the progress ring.
7. Notes on Dynamic Type handling — which text roles should scale (including the deliberately-large captions role) and which must stay fixed.
</what_to_give_me>

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS design engineer who specializes in editorial, commerce-forward marketplace interfaces — someone who builds pages that read like a printed record sleeve rather than a typical dark streaming dashboard, and who treats purchase UI as a first-class, non-buried affordance.

<reference_data>
Color tokens:
- Canvas (light, primary identity): #FFFFFF; grouped/elevated surface: #F4F4F4; pressed/hover: #EDEDED; divider: #E2E2E2
- Single brand accent (links, price, buy button, active states): #1DA0C3, a teal; a muted deep-teal variant #629AA9 for secondary/visited links; pressed state #17819E
- Dark mode is a true inversion (not the default identity): canvas #101417, surface #1A2024, divider #2C353B, accent shifted lighter to #3DB5D6 for contrast
- Text ink (not pure black): #1A1A1A; text secondary: #767676; text tertiary: #9A9A9A
- Success: #4CAF50; error: #E45858; warning: #E0A030

Typography ladder: a clean humanist sans (document as "DM Sans"). Screen titles 32pt/700; primary content title 22pt/700; section headers 22pt/700; an artist/creator link role specifically at 18pt/600 always in the accent color; body 16pt/400 with generous 1.55 line height; a price figure role at 22pt/700; a price-unit/hint role at 13pt/600; row/list titles 15pt/600; metadata 14pt/400; small track-name role 14pt/500 (upgrading to 700 + accent color when actively playing); tiny tabular index/caption role 12pt/600 with slight tracking; tab labels 10pt/600; buttons 15pt/700.

Spacing & geometry: 4pt base unit, scale 4/8/12/16/20/24/32/40/48/64. Corner radii are deliberately RESTRAINED: 0pt for full-bleed cover art at the top of a detail page, 2-4pt for grid thumbnails and buttons, 6pt for the signature buy card and search field, 12pt for sheets/modals, full pill reserved only for rare small chips, true circle for the small inline play control and avatars. Screen horizontal inset 20pt.

Distinctive named patterns:
1. A buy/support card: a bordered (not shadowed) surface showing a price figure with a currency unit, an "or more / pay what you want" hint line, a full-width solid-accent purchase button, and a secondary text-link wishlist/save action beneath it.
2. Full-bleed, strictly-square (1:1) cover art at the very top of a detail page, touching the screen edges, never cropped to a circle and never tinted/overlaid for contrast.
3. A social collection/activity feed: cards reading as "{person} acquired {item}" with cover, title, creator, and an optional personal note from the person who bought it.
4. An inline, banded (not card-shadowed) player strip: small circular play button, title/time readout, and a small waveform-style scrubber where the played portion is solid accent color and the unplayed portion is the same hue at low opacity.
5. A numbered tracklist with hairline row dividers where the currently-playing row's title switches to bold accent-colored text — no other row decoration.
6. Structural surfaces are separated by 1pt hairline borders and surface-color steps, never by drop shadows — the page stays flat and paper-like.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. The canvas is light and editorial by default — this is NOT a dark-first app; dark mode exists only as a true, deliberate inversion, never the default identity.
2. The single brand accent is scarce and meaningful: reserve it strictly for creator/artist links, the price figure's supporting elements, the purchase button, and "you own/follow this" states — never tint generic chrome or decorative UI with it.
3. Every content detail page must lead with a clear purchase affordance (price + pay-what-you-want-style hint + a solid-accent buy button) — this is a commerce app first, not a passive streaming surface, so the buy action is never hidden behind a secondary tab or icon.
4. Cover/content art is always a strict 1:1 square, full-bleed at the top of a detail page, and is NEVER cropped to a circle, tinted, or overlaid with a gradient for legibility — the uploaded artwork stays sovereign and untouched.
5. Use hairline borders and surface-color steps to organize zones — do not reach for drop shadows to separate a card from the page; the one narrow exception is a system bottom sheet, which may use a shadow to signal its temporary/dismissible nature.
6. Corner radii stay small and restrained throughout (single digits to low double digits) — do not default to large radii or full pill shapes on primary buttons; a pill is reserved only for small chips.
7. A social "collection/activity" feed of what people have acquired is a primary navigation destination, not a buried history screen — treat it as core identity, alongside the marketplace/detail surfaces.
8. Set body and description text with a generous line height and a comfortable reading measure — long-form artist/creator notes should feel like reading a printed sleeve, not a cramped app screen.
9. Use tabular numerals everywhere a number needs to align in a column — track indices, durations, prices, and player time readouts.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name and one-line pitch:
- Target iOS version and minimum device width:
- Primary content type being sold/streamed (music, courses, digital goods — describe it):
- Do you support a "pay what you want" / flexible pricing model, or fixed pricing only?
- What's your single brand accent hex, if different from the reference teal?
- Do you want a social "who bought/collected what" feed as a primary tab?
- Names of your primary navigation tabs (how many, and what do they represent)?
- Any currency/locale considerations for the price display?
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete SwiftUI `Color` extension and `Font` extension implementing the token ladder above, adapted to my project's inputs.
2. A detail/album-page SwiftUI view: full-bleed square cover, title/creator-link stack, and the signature buy/support card.
3. The buy/support card component itself, with price, hint text, purchase button, and secondary wishlist link specified precisely.
4. An inline banded player strip component (play button, title/time, waveform-style scrubber).
5. A numbered content-list (tracklist-equivalent) component with the playing-row accent-and-bold state specified.
6. A social collection/activity feed card component.
7. A short design-QA checklist covering accent scarcity (where it should and shouldn't appear), corner-radius consistency, and border-vs-shadow usage.
</what_to_give_me>

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS design engineer specializing in dark, gradient-accented music-player interfaces where a single vivid gradient must be rationed as a scarce visual resource against a quiet, near-monochrome chrome layer.

<reference_data>
Color tokens:
- Canvas: #0F0D13 — a violet-tinted near-black, deliberately never pure black, and there is no true light theme (only an OS-forced light fallback)
- Surface 1: #19161F; surface 2: #221E2B; divider: #2A2633
- Two-stop brand gradient running purple-to-pink: start #A238FF, end #FF0092 — used for the primary play button, scrubber fill, a feature badge, and generative artwork; either endpoint hue may be used solo for small icon fills or an active tab
- Pressed states: deep purple #7C28C4, deep pink #D60079
- Text primary: #FFFFFF; text secondary: #A29CB0; text tertiary: #6E6880
- Success: #1ED760; error: #FF4D5E; warning: #FFB02E

Typography ladder: a geometric sans (document as "Deezer Sans" with Inter as fallback). Screen titles 32pt/800; now-playing title 26pt/800; section headers 22pt/700; subheads 18pt/700; body (reading-weight, fallback family) 16pt/400; row titles 15pt/600; now-playing artist line 15pt/500; metadata 14pt/400; an uppercase tracked overline role at 12pt/700 with ~0.4pt tracking for context labels above hero artwork; scrubber time 11pt/500 tabular; tab labels 10pt/600; buttons 16pt/700; chips 13pt/700.

Spacing & geometry: 4pt base unit, scale 4/8/12/16/20/22/24/28/32/40/48/64. Corner radii: 4pt for the scrubber track and equalizer-bar tops, 6pt for row-thumbnail art, 8pt for inline cards, 12pt for search/sheets, 16pt as the signature radius for the primary hero artwork tile, full pill for all buttons/chips/the feature badge, true circle for the play button/avatars. Screen horizontal inset is generous at 24pt.

Distinctive named patterns:
1. A living-gradient hero artwork tile (not a static photo) representing a personalized/generative mix — a multi-stop gradient with a soft white bloom and a deep-tone bloom, slowly drifting while that content plays, badged with a small pill in the corner.
2. An embedded equalizer rendered directly INSIDE the hero artwork tile itself (a row of bars pinned to its bottom edge) rather than as a separate visualizer panel — the cover art doubles as the visualizer.
3. A now-playing-aware song row: the row for the currently-playing item recolors its title into the gradient's end hue and swaps its trailing icon for a small live equalizer indicator.

<house_rules>
1. The canvas must be a tinted near-black, never a true #000000 — the tint is what keeps the gradient feeling like it belongs to the same color world as the background rather than being pasted on top.
2. The two-stop brand gradient is scarce by design — restrict it to the primary play button, the scrubber fill, one feature/context badge, and generative hero artwork; never spread it across headers, cards, or general backgrounds.
3. All secondary/structural chrome (chevrons, secondary transport controls, inactive tab icons, dividers) must stay in a single neutral tone — color belongs only to things tied directly to active playback or the personalized-mix feature.
4. Any "visualizer" or equalizer element belongs embedded inside the relevant artwork tile itself, not rendered as a separate panel — treat the artwork as reactive content, not a static image with UI floating over it.
5. The now-playing state has one specific accent color (the gradient's end hue) reserved for it in list rows — reusing the gradient's start hue for "now playing" is a mistake; keep the two hues' roles distinct.
6. Never use a grey Material-style drop shadow on this canvas — it will be invisible against near-black; every shadow in this system must be a colored ambient glow drawn from the gradient's hues.
7. Titles are set heavy by default (bold to heavy weights) — thin or light weights fail against this dark, quiet canvas and undermine the confident brand voice.
8. Geometry defaults to full-pill for interactive controls (buttons, chips, badges) alongside one larger, non-pill radius reserved specifically for the primary hero artwork tile — don't blend these roles.
9. Any equalizer/visualizer animation must freeze immediately on pause and only animate while audio is actually playing — never let a "reactive" element animate independent of real playback state.
</house_rules>

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS design engineer specializing in live-broadcast audio interfaces — someone who understands that a live stream has fundamentally different controls than an on-demand track (no seeking, no pause, no elapsed/remaining time) and designs the transport accordingly.

<reference_data>
Color tokens:
- Canvas: #120A0E — a warm maroon-black, deliberately never a true pure black; there is no full light theme for the player, only an OS-forced fallback
- Surface 1: #1E1216; surface 2: #2A171D; divider: #341C24
- Primary brand red (play button, logomark fill, primary CTAs): #C6002B; a distinct coral reserved exclusively for "live" signaling (badge, scanning sweep, live tags, active tab): #F23A2F; a magenta gradient-end accent for shelf headers/highlights: #E40A5D; pressed states #9E0022 (red) and #CC2D24 (coral)
- Text primary: #FFFFFF; text secondary: #B8A0A8; text tertiary: #7C6168
- Success: #1ED760; error: #FF4D5E; warning: #FFB02E

Typography ladder: a geometric sans (document as "iHeart Sans" with Inter as fallback). Screen titles 32pt/800; station/show name 26pt/800; section headers 22pt/700; subheads 18pt/700; body 16pt/400; row titles 15pt/600; a "now airing" metadata line 15pt/500; general metadata 14pt/400; a LIVE tag/overline role at an unusually heavy 12pt/900 with ~0.8pt tracking for broadcast-poster energy; a frequency/callsign chip role 12pt/800; tab labels 10pt/600; buttons 16pt/700; chips 13pt/700.

Spacing & geometry: 4pt base unit, scale 4/8/12/16/20/22/24/28/32/40/48/64. Corner radii: 4pt for the scanning-bar track, 8pt for station-row logo tiles and small chips, 12pt for search/sheets, 14pt for the primary station-tile artwork, 16pt for hero shelf cards, full pill for all buttons/chips/the LIVE badge, true circle for the play button/avatars/the pulsing live-dot. Screen horizontal inset is generous at 24pt.

Distinctive named patterns:
1. A scanning bar that REPLACES the scrubber entirely for live content — an indeterminate colored sweep animating left-to-right across a thin track, with no knob, no elapsed time, and no remaining time, because a live broadcast cannot be seeked.
2. Stop-not-pause transport — the center playback control toggles between play and a square stop glyph (never a pause glyph), and the flanking prev/next controls perform station-skip rather than track-skip, reinforcing that you join/leave a broadcast rather than pausing it.
3. A pulsing "LIVE" badge: a small pill in the reserved live-signal color containing a radiating dot that continuously pulses on a slow loop plus the word "LIVE" in a very heavy weight — the single most "alive"-feeling element in the interface.
4. A brand-logomark artwork fallback: when a live station has no real cover art, a centered brand logomark rendered on a warm radially-lit gradient tile stands in as the artwork.
5. A frequency/callsign glass chip overlaid on the artwork tile, giving quick-glance station identity independent of the metadata below it.
6. Strict color rationing between two closely related brand hues: one is the general structural action color (play button, logomark, CTAs), the other is reserved exclusively as the unambiguous "this is live" signal color and must never be reused for anything else.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. The canvas must be a warm, tinted near-black, never a true pure black — the warmth signals "broadcast"/warmth rather than a generic dark-mode screen.
2. Maintain strict separation between the two brand hues: the structural action color drives the play button and general CTAs, while the second, distinct hue is reserved exclusively for "this is live right now" signaling and must never bleed into non-live UI.
3. Any live-stream player must NEVER show a scrubber, a progress knob, or elapsed/remaining timestamps — replace all of that with an indeterminate scanning-sweep indicator, since seeking a live broadcast is not a real capability.
4. The center transport control for live content is a play/stop toggle, never play/pause — and prev/next controls must be understood and labeled as station-skip, not track-skip.
5. The "LIVE" indicator must continuously pulse/animate for as long as the stream is genuinely live — never let this animation run when the content is not actually live, and never let it go static while truly live.
6. When there is no real cover art for a piece of content (as with a live station), fall back to a branded logomark on a warm gradient tile rather than a blank or generic placeholder square.
7. Never use a grey Material-style drop shadow on this canvas — it will be invisible against the near-black; use colored ambient glows drawn from the primary red hue instead.
8. Titles and LIVE tags default to very heavy weights (bold through the heaviest available weight) — thin or light weights undermine the broadcast-poster energy this system depends on.
9. Keep all secondary/structural chrome (chevrons, secondary transport, inactive tab icons) in a single neutral tone — color is reserved for the play button, the logomark, and anything explicitly signaling "live."
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name and one-line pitch:
- Target iOS version and minimum device width:
- Do you serve live/broadcast content, on-demand content, or both? Describe the mix:
- If you have live content, what should the transport controls do when no seeking is possible?
- What are your primary and "live-signal" accent hex colors, if different from the reference red/coral?
- Do you have real artwork for all content, or do you need a logomark/branded-tile fallback like the reference?
- Names of your primary navigation tabs (how many, and what do they represent)?
- Any station/channel metadata (like a frequency or callsign) you want displayed on the artwork tile?
</the_project>

2. A full-screen live-player SwiftUI view: warm canvas, artwork/logomark tile with a pulsing LIVE badge and metadata chip, the scanning-bar component (no scrubber), and the play/stop + station-skip transport row.

4. A live-content-aware list row component distinguishing live items from any on-demand items in the same list.
5. A bottom tab bar and mini-player bar implementation consistent with the token set.
6. A short design-QA checklist verifying the two-hue rationing rule and confirming no scrubber/timestamp ever appears on live content.

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS design engineer specializing in restrained, single-developer-caliber audio apps — someone who defaults to the native system font, one disciplined accent color, flat editorial chrome, and exposes power features directly on the main screen rather than burying them in settings.

<reference_data>
Color tokens:
- Light canvas (the signature identity): #FBFAF6 — a warm paper-cream, explicitly not stark white; light surface: #F7F5EF; light pressed: #EDEBE3; light divider: #E4E1D8
- Dark canvas: #121212; dark surface 1: #1C1C1E; dark surface 2: #2A2A2C; dark divider: #303032
- Single accent (identical across both themes): #FC7E0F, a warm orange; pressed #E06A00
- A secondary link-blue (#2D7FF9) reserved for external web links only — the brand accent is preferred for all in-app actions
- Text primary/secondary/tertiary defined separately for light (#1A1A1A / #6E6E6E / #9A9A9A) and dark (#F2F2F2 / #9A9A9A / #6A6A6A)
- Success: #34C759; error: #FF3B30; warning: #FF9F0A
- A small set of rounded-square playlist-icon tints (the accent orange plus a blue, a green, and a purple) for distinguishing smart-playlist categories

Typography ladder: 100% the native system font (document with Inter as a documentation fallback). Large nav title 32pt/800; a now-playing episode-title role 22pt/700; section headers 22pt/700; detail-view titles 18pt/700; list-row titles 15pt/600; body 16pt/400; a show/creator-name sub-role 14pt/500; general metadata 14pt/400; a one-line description role 12pt/400; a rare uppercase tracked "stat" caption at 12pt/600 (used specifically for a running achievement-style counter); tabular timecodes at 12pt/500; buttons 16pt/600; toggle labels 15pt/600; small effect-row chip labels 10pt/600; tab labels 10pt/600.

Spacing & geometry: 4pt base unit, scale 4/8/12/16/20/24/28/32/40/48/64. Corner radii: 4pt for scrubber track/small badges, 8pt for row-artwork thumbnails, 9-10pt for playlist icon tiles/buttons/search field/cover art, 14pt for bottom sheets, 20pt for large modal sheets, full pill reserved for a rate/speed readout and occasional chips, true circle for the play-ring/avatars/small inline play controls.

Distinctive named patterns:
1. An outlined circular play button rendered as a stroked ring (not a filled disc) — a specific, deliberately unusual choice that is the single most recognizable control in the whole system, used both at large size on the player and smaller on individual content rows.
2. Skip-interval buttons that display the actual numeric interval as part of the glyph itself (the number sits directly beneath a chevron-pair icon), rather than a generic unlabeled skip icon.
3. Two first-class audio-processing toggles surfaced directly in the player's main control row (not buried in settings): one that shortens silences in spoken-word audio without altering pitch, and one that applies loudness/EQ tuned specifically for speech clarity.
4. A running "time saved" achievement-style counter tied to the silence-shortening feature, displayed as a rare uppercase tracked caption — a deliberate, visible badge of the feature's value rather than a hidden statistic.
5. A playlists-as-home-surface pattern: smart (rule-based) and manual playlists rendered as tidy rows with a colored rounded-square icon, a name, a one-line description, and a trailing item count — this list, not a content grid, is the app's primary landing surface.
6. A social recommendation feed: users can publicly recommend individual pieces of content, and a feed surfaces friends' recommendations with avatars and optional short notes — a differentiator most competitor apps in this category don't have.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. The light-mode canvas must be a warm, paper-like off-white, never stark pure white — this warmth is the single most identity-defining visual choice in the whole system.
2. There is exactly one accent color, held identical across both light and dark themes — never introduce a second brand hue, and reserve the accent strictly for action (the play control, active toggles, links, active tab, primary buttons), never for decorative use.
3. The primary play button must be rendered as an outlined ring (a stroke, not a fill) — this is a deliberate, load-bearing brand signature; filling the button solid is a wrong implementation, not a stylistic variant.
4. Any content-processing/enhancement toggles this app offers (speed normalization, clarity boosting, or equivalents) must be first-class controls directly on the main playback screen — never bury them two levels deep in a settings screen.
5. If a feature produces a measurable benefit over time (like accumulated time saved), surface a running counter for it as a small point of pride, using the rare uppercase-tracked caption style reserved for exactly this kind of stat.
6. Skip-interval controls must show their actual numeric interval as part of the control's visual footprint, not as a separate unlabeled icon — the number is part of the glyph.
7. The primary navigation home surface is an organized list of curated/rule-based collections (not a content grid) — treat this list as equally important as, or more important than, a browse/discover grid.
8. Type hierarchy is expressed purely through size and weight, never through color — the single accent color is reserved for genuinely interactive/active elements, never used decoratively to indicate hierarchy.
9. Keep shadows minimal and purposeful: reserve visible drop shadows for the primary cover artwork and floating sheet surfaces only; list rows and grouped settings stay perfectly flat with hairline dividers.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name and one-line pitch:
- Target iOS version and minimum device width:
- Primary content type (podcasts, audiobooks, other long-form audio — describe your catalog):
- Do you have (or want) audio-processing features like silence-shortening or speech-clarity boosting? Describe them:
- What's your single accent hex, if different from the reference orange?
- Do you want a playlists/collections-first home surface, or a content-grid-first home surface?
- Do you want a social recommendation feature? Describe the intended sharing model:
- Names of your primary navigation tabs (how many, and what do they represent)?
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete SwiftUI `Color` extension and system-font-based `Font` styles implementing the token ladder above, adapted to my project's inputs.
2. A full-screen player SwiftUI view: warm/paper canvas, cover art, the signature outlined-ring play button, labeled skip buttons, scrubber, and an effects row (processing toggles + any speed control).
3. The two processing-toggle rows (or your equivalent features) with their labels, descriptions, and switch styling specified.
4. A playlist/collection row component with colored rounded-square icon, description, and trailing count.
5. A bottom tab bar and mini-player bar implementation consistent with the token set.
6. A recommendation-feed card component (if applicable to my project) with avatar, name, content reference, and optional note.
7. A short design-QA checklist verifying the play-ring-never-filled rule, accent scarcity, and flat/hairline-divider discipline on lists.
</what_to_give_me>
